newsitem.title: USA: LCI Intl CEO says should meet EPS estimates.
newsitem.headline: LCI Intl CEO says should meet EPS estimates.

text.p: LCI International chairman and chief executive H. Brian Thompson said Thursday the fast-growing long distance telephone company is "in good shape" to meet Wall Street's earnings estimates for the remainder of the year.

Thompson, in an interview with Reuters, said he remains "very bullish" about the LCI's future prospects, particularly in light of strong second quarter earnings reported late Wednesday. LCI reported revenue, operating income and net income growth rates of 20 percent or more from a year ago.

Unless the company is involved in a second half acquisition, "I see no reaon why we shouldn't" match consensus estimates given that operating margins are expected to remain in the 18-to-20 percent range, he said.
Thompson declined to offer details regarding possible acquisitions, but said "we are always" in talks about acquisitions.

The First Call consensus earnings per share estimates for the third quarter is $0.27 versus $0.23 a year ago; for the fourth quarter is $0.28 versus $0.24 last year; and for fiscal 1997 is $1.03 versus $0.85 in 1996.

Thompson said he expects continued growth to remain balanced across all of the company's business segments: residential and commercial long distance (both domestic and international) and local phone service.
LCI hopes to be offering local phone service in 30 U.S. markets by year end, he said, up from the current 22.
